newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Marcos appeal against jail term thrown out.
newsitem.headline: Marcos appeal against jail term thrown out.

text.p: A Philippine court on Wednesday rejected an appeal by former first lady Imelda Marcos against a 1993 ruling sentencing her to 18 years in jail for corruption, leaving her with one last chance to avoid imprisonment.
The three judges of Manila's anti-graft court voted unanimously to dismiss "for lack of merit" her motion for reconsideration, the court said in its ruling.
The decision left the 67-year-old widow of late president Ferdinand Marcos with only one recourse to avoid going to jail -- an appeal to the Supreme Court whose verdict is final.
The Supreme Court is required under the constitution to make a decision in two years. In the meantime, the anti-graft court ruled that Marcos could remain free on bail.

A Marcos aide said the former first lady was still waiting for an official copy of the verdict and had no immediate reaction. But she is expected to elevate her case to the Supreme Court, court sources said.

Marcos was convicted of breaking anti-corruption laws by unlawfully leasing state property in 1982 to a medical foundation she headed under terms which the court said were grossly unfair to the government.

Besides rejecting Marcos's appeal, the anti-graft court also ordered her and a co-accused, Jose Dans, a transportation minister in the Marcos government, to pay the government 124.4 million pesos ($4.8 million) in damages.
The amount corresponds to the sum of money which the court said the government lost in the lease.
Dans had joined Marcos in the appeal but the anti-graft court also rejected his plea for a reconsideration.

The Marcoses were overthrown in a popular revolt in 1986 and fled to Hawaii. After her husband died there in 1989, Imelda Marcos was allowed to return and last year won a seat in the House of Representatives.
Marcos still faces dozens of criminal and civil court actions arising from her husband's 20-year rule.
